newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend fall, seen flat on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend fall, seen flat on Thursday.

text.p: Polish shares extended Tuesday's fall but analysts said the market might have put the bulk of its profit-taking correction behind it after surging 27 percent since December 10 on apparent heightened foreign demand.

All the bourse's banks fell on Wednesday, with many extending losses after the central bank's Monday decision to raise mandatory reserves on zloty call and currency deposits, and analysts said some banks would fall again Thursday.
"Prices should remain around current levels but I wouldn't expect growth from that branch (banks)," said Krzysztof Olszewski, an analyst at Bank Slaski brokerage.
The main market's all-share WIG index fell 2.3 percent to 16,299.0 points and turnover eased 4.2 percent to 213 million zlotys on both markets.
Analysts said significant falls by some banks, such as Kredyt Bank which tumbled 8.1 percent, suggested that some banks would soon rebound.
"It seems if somebody wanted to sell (a bank) he did so already, their falls were so big," said Pawel Dmytryk, a trader at Bank Staropolski brokerage.
Among big losers WBK fell six percent, PPABank 5.4 percent and BPH 4.8 percent.

Optimus, the main market's biggest loser, fell 9.8 percent in profit-taking, extending Tuesday's fall after surging over 100 percent this month in part on good 1996 earnings which the firm says it might repeat this year.
Continuous trade turnover was at 36.2 million zlotys with 11 stocks down and six flat.
NFI units fell 2.6 percent to 150 zlotys in 29.3-million-zloty regular bourse trade and rose 0.3 percent to 148.5 zlotys in 28.5-million-zloty continuous trade.
